findings.who: A filer whose 2024 investment interest was more than their 2024 net investment income, but who filed no 2024 Form 4952. They took the standard deduction, believed the form was not required, or a preparer left it off.
findings.why_no: The outer question asks whether they 'have investment interest expense carried forward from an earlier year'. With no 2024 Form 4952 and no deduction claimed, they believe nothing was 'disallowed' or 'carried forward' and answer no. The inner question's 'what line 7 of a correct 2024 Form 4952 would show' never appears, because the outer no stops the gate first.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 1, line 7: 'Disallowed investment interest expense to be carried forward to 2026. Subtract line 6 from line 3'; line 2: 'Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7'
findings.fix: Move the fact-based wording into the outer question: 'In 2024 or an earlier year, did you or your spouse have interest on money borrowed for investments (including margin interest or interest shown on a Schedule K-1) that was more than your investment income, even if you filed no Form 4952 or took the standard deduction?'

findings.who: A filer whose only investment interest in 2024 was margin interest on a brokerage statement, or investment interest passed through on a partnership or S corporation Schedule K-1. Some of it was disallowed on the 2024 Form 4952 that their software or preparer produced.
findings.why_no: They never 'borrowed money for investments' in their own view. The K-1 interest was the entity's, and margin is an account feature. The words 'investment interest expense carried forward' do not match anything they remember, so they answer no to both clauses.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: 'Include investment interest expense reported to you on Schedule K-1 from a partnership or an S corporation'; p. 1, line 2
findings.fix: Name the sources in the gate: 'margin interest on a brokerage account, investment interest shown on a Schedule K-1, or other interest on loans used to buy investments'. Also tell the filer to check line 7 of any 2024 Form 4952 in their return, including forms the software or preparer produced.

findings.who: A filer whose disallowed investment interest arose in 2022 or 2023 and is still unused. Their 2024 return omitted Form 4952 because they had no new investment interest in 2024.
findings.why_no: The gate's line label reads 'Investment interest expense disallowed in 2024 and carried forward'. They had no investment interest in 2024, so nothing was disallowed that year, and they answer no.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Who Must File: 'You don't have any carryover of disallowed investment interest expense from 2024'; p. 1, line 7 (carryforward is line 3, which includes line 2's prior carryover, less line 6)
findings.fix: Relabel the gate: 'Investment interest expense disallowed in 2024 or any earlier year and not yet deducted'. State in the outer question that a carryover can persist through years with no new interest and no Form 4952 filed.

findings.who: Any filer shown the outer question. The question ends 'Answer Yes if any of these applies:' but its list does not appear in the gate as reviewed.
findings.why_no: If the list names only current-year borrowing, such as margin loans, a filer with only a carryforward may read the list as the whole rule and answer no.
findings.fix: Make sure the list includes a separate item: 'investment interest you could not deduct in an earlier year (line 7 of a prior Form 4952, or an amount that should have been there)'.

p. 1, Part I, line 2, "Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7"; p. 3, Who Must File, "You don’t have any carryover of disallowed investment interest expense from 2024"

findings.who: A limited partner or S corporation shareholder whose Schedule K-1 reports investment interest expense; the partnership or S corporation borrowed and paid the interest, not the filer.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether you paid interest on money borrowed to buy investments. The filer did not pay it—the entity did—so they answer no even though the K-1 reports the amount.
findings.line: f4952.line1_if_interest, and f4952.carryover_if_interest if the K-1 amount was disallowed in 2024
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: 'Include investment interest expense reported to you on Schedule K-1 from a partnership or an S corporation.'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to ask whether you or your spouse paid or accrued investment interest, received a Schedule K-1 reporting investment interest expense, or have a carryforward.

findings.who: An individual on the accrual method who accrued investment interest in 2025 on a loan used to buy investments but did not pay it by year-end.
findings.why_no: The gate asks 'did you pay interest'; the filer did not pay, only accrued it.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: 'Enter the investment interest expense paid or accrued during the tax year...'
findings.fix: Use 'paid or accrued' in the gate, not just 'pay'.

findings.who: A filer whose loan proceeds were split between buying investments and personal or home use; the filer reads the question as asking only about a loan borrowed wholly to buy investments.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'money borrowed to buy investments' and the help says 'if the money went into investments'; the filer thinks a mixed-use loan is not an investment loan.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Allocation of Interest Expense: 'If you paid or accrued interest on a loan and used the loan proceeds for more than one purpose, you may have to allocate the interest.'
findings.fix: Ask 'Was any part of a loan used to buy investments?' and state at the gate that only the investment share counts.

findings.who: A filer who borrowed to buy a direct working interest in an oil or gas property and did not materially participate; the filer views it as a business, not an investment.
findings.why_no: The gate asks about money borrowed to buy 'investments,' with a broker margin loan as the example; a working interest sounds like a trade or business.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Property held for investment: 'A working interest in an oil or gas property that you held directly or through an entity that didn’t limit your liability is property held for investment, but only if you didn’t materially participate in the activity.'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to include a non-materially-participated oil or gas working interest, or ask about 'property held for investment' with examples beyond broker margin.

findings.who: A filer with a 2024 Form 4952 line 7 carryover but no 2025 interest payment; the filer focuses on the current year and does not connect the carryover to interest paid in an earlier year.
findings.why_no: The gate asks 'In 2025 ... did you pay interest'; the filer did not pay in 2025 and treats the old carryover as not relevant.
findings.line: f4952.carryover_if_interest, and f4952.line1_if_interest if the carryover allows a current deduction
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 1, Part I, line 2: 'Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7.'
findings.fix: Explicitly include carryforward in the gate: '...or does either of you have investment interest expense carried forward from an earlier year?'

findings.who: A filer with a home-equity loan whose proceeds were used to buy investments; the interest is reported on Form 1098 as mortgage interest.
findings.why_no: The gate's example is a margin loan from a broker, so the filer thinks home-equity interest is home mortgage interest, not investment interest.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Allocation of Interest Expense: 'If you paid or accrued interest on a loan and used the loan proceeds for more than one purpose, you may have to allocate the interest'; p. 3, Line 1 excludes 'Personal interest under section 163(h), including qualified residence interest.'
findings.fix: State at the gate that any loan counts, including a home-equity loan, to the extent its proceeds were used to buy investments; ask for the investment share.

findings.who: A filer who paid investment interest in 2025 but has no ordinary investment income, only qualified dividends or long-term gains; the filer thinks there is no deduction and answers no.
findings.why_no: The filer reads the gate as asking whether there is a current deductible investment interest expense; since net investment income is zero, they say no.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 4, Line 4g: 'To make the election, enter on line 4g the amount you elect to include in investment income'; p. 1, line 7: 'Disallowed investment interest expense to be carried forward to 2026.'
findings.fix: State that interest paid is reported even if no current deduction is allowed and even if the only possible deduction depends on a line 4g election; ask about qualified dividends and long-term gains at the gate or before zeroing line 4g.

findings.who: A filer who paid investment interest but meets the Form 4952 exception because investment income from interest and ordinary dividends exceeds the interest, there are no other investment expenses, and there is no 2024 carryover.
findings.why_no: The filer reads the gate as asking whether they must file Form 4952; the instructions say they don't have to file, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Who Must File, Exception: 'You don’t have to file Form 4952 if all of the following apply. • Your investment income from interest and ordinary dividends minus any qualified dividends is more than your investment interest expense. • You don’t have any other deductible investment expenses. • You don’t have any carryover...'
findings.fix: Separate 'did you pay investment interest' from 'must file Form 4952'; if the exception applies, still capture line 1 for the Schedule A deduction.
